newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines seen buying wheat, corn on price dips.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seen buying wheat, corn on price dips.

text.p: Philippine grain importers are expected to be in the market for wheat and corn in the coming week if prices dip to "reasonable" levels, government and trade officials said on Friday.

"Philippine flour millers may likely buy wheat for their March requirements if the price of dark northern spring and western white wheat in the United States fall from present levels," said an executive in one of the country's largest flour millers.
Philippine firms were also offered wheat by other suppliers from Australia and Argentina, traders said.
"We are now looking for suppliers for our March requirement. However, at present prices of U.S. wheat we would rather stay on the sidelines unless given attractive offers," the miller said.

On Thursday, Philippine flour millers Delta Milling Corp and Morning Star Corp bought 13,000 tonnes of U.S. western white wheat from Mitsubishi Corp and another 3,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat from U.S. trading giant Cargill, traders said. The commodity is for February shipment.

They also said Philippine firms bought 29,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat at $3.94 per bushel from a U.S. port and 6,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $3.90 per bushel on January 17. The wheat is also for February delivery.

The state-agency Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing price of hard flour dropped to 290 pesos per 25 kg bag from last week's 295 pesos while the price of soft flour was steady at 260 pesos per kg.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero also said the Philippines is negotiating to buy corn for livestock and poultry raisers.
Manila traders said early this week the Philippines bought about 145,000 tonnes of Chinese corn but the government declined to confirm it saying negotiations for the deal were still on.
"We are still negotiating on a government-to-government basis. The volume will depend on the price China is willing to sell to us," Escudero said in an earlier interview.

The state-agency National Food Authority said the average retail price of yellow corn increased to 10.53 pesos per kg from last week's 10.41 pesos while white corn increased to 11.11 pesos per kg from last week's 10.74 pesos.
